title: The Land of Toys
author: Enid Blyton
description: Join three children and their magical friends on a fun adventure to the Land of Toys!

sets.title: Chapter 1: The Saucepan Man Brings News
sets.passage:
One day, the Saucepan Man visits Joe, Beth, and Franny to share exciting news. He tells them that a new land called the Land of Toys is coming to the top of the Faraway Tree the next morning. The Saucepan Man wears so many clanking pots and pans that he can hardly hear a word, so when Beth says "we'll have fun", he beams and asks for a bun instead.

The next day, the children climb the enormous Faraway Tree in the middle of the wood. On their way up, the tree grows blackberries and then pine cones. Finally, they reach Moonface's house at the top and enjoy magical 'Well-I-Never' rolls, which change flavors with every bite.

choices: Moonface

questions.explanation: The Saucepan Man visits Joe, Beth, and Franny at their house to tell them about the Land of Toys coming to the top of the tree.

choices: Very old
Very big
Very fast
Very quiet
questions.explanation: "Enormous" means extremely large or huge, describing how tall and thick the tree was.

Blackberries

choices: The children buy toy soldiers from a market.
The children get lost in a dark forest.

sets.title: Chapter 2: The Land of Toys
sets.passage:
The group climbs up the ladder into the cloud and enters the Land of Toys. To their surprise, the toys in the village are all alive, walking around, and as big as the children.

Moonface and the Saucepan Man push a Wobbly Man over, and he is so upset that he goes straight to the Toy Soldier Captain to report them. Then Joe pulls a knob on a toy cannon by the wooden fort, and it goes off with a loud bang that frightens the village toys. The travelers are brought before the angry Captain, who orders them about in a loud, commanding voice. When fifty wooden soldiers try to take them to the dungeon, Joe pushes one soldier, causing the entire row to fall like dominoes. To avoid punishment, everyone cleverly pretends to be Clockwork toys.

questions.prompt: What surprises the children when they arrive in the Land of Toys?
choices: The toys are made of real gold.
The toys are alive and as big as humans.
The village is completely empty.
All the toys are broken.
questions.explanation: When they reach the village, they notice teddy bears and dolls walking around and being as big as the children.

questions.prompt: Why does the Wobbly Man report the visitors to the Toy Soldier Captain?
choices: Because they stole his hat.
Because they pushed him over and upset him.
Because they refused to eat his food.
Because they lost their way in the village.
questions.explanation: The Saucepan Man and Moonface push the Wobbly Man over, which angers him enough to report them to the Captain.

questions.prompt: What happens when Joe pulls the knob on the toy cannon at the fort?
choices: It plays a merry song.
It fires with a loud bang and frightens the village toys.
It turns into a clockwork clown.
It shoots colorful fireworks into the sky.
questions.explanation: Joe pulls the knob on the cannon, causing it to go off with a loud bang and frighten the villagers.

questions.prompt: What does the word "commanding" mean when describing the Captain's voice?
choices: Soft and quiet
Strong and giving orders
Confused and worried
Funny and silly
questions.explanation: "Commanding" describes a firm, authoritative tone used when giving orders.

questions.prompt: How do the fifty toy soldiers fall down all at once?
choices: Joe uses a magic spell.
The Captain orders them to lie down.
Joe pushes one soldier, knocking them all over like dominoes.
A strong wind blows them down.
questions.explanation: Joe pushes the nearest wooden soldier, who knocks down the next soldier, creating a domino effect that knocks down all fifty soldiers.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of Chapter 2?
choices: The visitors get into silly trouble in Toyland but escape the dungeon by acting like toys.
The Saucepan Man finds his aunt and buys many presents.
The Toy Soldiers capture Moonface and force him to build a fort.
The children decide to live in the wooden tower forever.
questions.explanation: Chapter 2 recounts how the travelers cause accidental trouble in Toyland and escape being locked in a dungeon by tricking the Captain into thinking they are toys.
